target.title: Final Fantasy XIV 1.23b
target.notes: The target is frozen. No other 1.x version is a support target, and version is metadata, never a tooling branch key.

platforms.notes: Built and tested only while a hosted runner for this architecture exists.

formats.name: Resource ID to DAT path mapping
formats.notes: The id to data/AA/BB/CC/DD.DAT mapping is total over the 32-bit space, both directions, with public cases for the mapping and for malformed identifiers. The catalog CLI derives an id only from a matching path and otherwise records null; public CLI tests cover known, malformed, and unknown DAT rows plus deterministic ordering. Bounded catalog extraction accepts only explicit IDs or paths, validates catalog uniqueness, path containment, source identity, count and byte limits, and complete serial extraction plans before output. Public CLI tests cover JSON and JSONL input, duplicate and missing selections, ambiguous catalog identities, stale metadata, traversal and link refusal, overflow and limits, mixed unsupported or malformed resources, isolated collision-safe outputs, and determinism. Confirmed against retail 1.23b: all 140180 install resources match the convention. Stays supported rather than verified because the operation takes an identifier listing, so no retail file is a fixture for it. Evidence: docs/formats/sedb-res.md.

formats.name: SEDB container
formats.notes: Header and bounded enumeration only. The 0x10 field is advisory, not a container extent: across the install it equals the file size for 92303 of 97749 SEDB resources, headerSize for the 5203 PHB, zero for the 145 mtb, and a sub-file extent for 98 vins and leaf. Opt-in extraction copies an unambiguous direct-root payload span exactly and records its source range, digest, and entry relationship; public CLI tests cover exact bytes, deterministic output, empty spans, truncation, and option boundaries. Payload interpretation, unknownA, and flags are unresolved and reported rather than guessed. Standalone SEDB parsing does not accept GTEX; PWIB is read separately and delegates its nested resource to this reader. Gaps: docs/formats/sedb-res.md.

formats.name: RES container
formats.notes: Extended header, subresource directory, nested containers, unknown gaps, and clamped over-long extents. Directory offsets are confirmed against retail 1.23b: subresources land on SEDB signatures at the headerSize + 16 * count payload base. Opt-in extraction writes exact direct-root subresources and gaps with deterministic names and relationship metadata, retaining nested containers once as their parent span. Public CLI tests cover nesting, overlap, complete alias, out-of-range, clamp, malformed nested input, empty spans, and determinism. Any span ambiguity fails with a typed error before output. Directory kind values and unknownB are unresolved, and the overlapping trailing region every RES carries is reported rather than resolved. Gaps: docs/formats/sedb-res.md.

formats.name: SQEX container
formats.notes: The container the client's UI resources are stored in: an eight-byte signature, then a body whose whole 64-bit blocks are enciphered under a key that is the file's own base name, with a final run shorter than a block left in the clear. The cipher is the published Blowfish algorithm with its block halves read as little-endian words, which is the part established against retail data rather than taken from the specification. Read completely: all 1155 SQEX containers in the install decipher to UTF-8 widget documents, re-enciphering reproduces every input byte, and the reading reports the container plus a census of the document's shape rather than its content. Public read cases cover both tail cases, a byte order mark, the two constructs the widget profile adds, and seven malformed inputs; eight private read cases cover all six suffixes against retail 1.23b. Supported export writes exact decoded document bytes through extract-resource with the original basename key, deterministic payload manifests, and exact source replay. Public extract cases and CLI tests cover byte preservation, tail boundaries, filename keying, malformed inputs, determinism, and verification failures. Export has no private-case parity claim. Not claimed: the widget markup's meaning, entity expansion, writing, and the GTEX and SPKL files stored beside these containers. Evidence: docs/formats/sqex.md.

formats.name: Scrambled XML document
formats.notes: An XML document behind a one-byte trailer, a partial byte reversal, and a two-key word cipher. Recognition is the decode itself, not the trailer byte: two resources in the install end in it and are not documents. The first word key is derived from the encoded length and the second is recovered from the document's own known opening, so nothing is stored and nothing is guessed. Read completely: all 799 scrambled resources in the install decode to well-formed UTF-8 XML, and a decoded document is handed to the same reader a plaintext one gets. Public read cases cover both document kinds, all four encoded-length residues, and five malformed inputs; private read cases cover all four residues against retail 1.23b, recorded by span, key, digest, and name census rather than by content. Supported export writes exact decoded document bytes through extract-resource and selected extract-catalog entries, with deterministic payload manifests, output accounting, and exact source replay. Public extract cases and CLI tests cover byte preservation, all four residues, malformed inputs, determinism, catalog extraction, and verification failures. Export has no private-case parity claim. Evidence: docs/formats/ssd-sheet.md.

formats.name: SSD master schema
formats.notes: The master document is a <ssd> root whose sheets are references: a name and the decimal resource id of the schema document that defines the sheet. Read completely, with every attribute preserved verbatim, and resolved to a DAT path through the resource-path mapping. Public cases cover the document and six malformed inputs. Stays supported rather than verified because a faithful report of a schema document is the document, so a committed expected output for a retail one would publish client data; retail parity is established instead by the non-gating census in tools/research/. Evidence: docs/formats/ssd-sheet.md.

formats.name: SSD sheet info and data
formats.notes: Supported read and CSV export cover the schema document, enable-driven row offsets, all ten retail column types, IEEE-754 binary16, rich strings, and the Chinese xtx/quest trailing-column omission. Public whole-directory cases and literal generated-tree CSV oracles cover explicit nonadjacent resource links, sparse rows, complete versus incomplete absent triples, trailing omissions, duplicate logical cells, determinism, and malformed linked sets. Standalone CSV cases cover binary16 and exact rich-token preservation. The recorded game-directory run discovered and exported 803 definition documents from retail 1.23b without a master list or third-party binary, matching the reference corpus's names, header shapes, and row counts. Direct cataloging confirmed that all 585 resources of 195 absent Chinese block triples are unshipped, and the comparison corpus leaves their unique columns empty. The recorded export retained 639 explicit missing markers and reported 57 conflicting duplicates. These public cases do not add private extraction parity. Write-back still needs round-trip fixtures. Evidence: docs/formats/ssd-sheet.md.

formats.name: Sparse enable-file row ranges
formats.notes: Pairs of first row identifier and run length, read completely, with an empty or out-of-order range reported as an anomaly rather than rejected and a trailing partial record failing cleanly. Retail 1.23b parity: across all 37 blocks the ranges name exactly the row slots whose offset entry carries a span, 533 ranges over 7866 rows. Evidence: docs/formats/ssd-sheet.md.

formats.name: Rich strings and control codes
formats.notes: Read is supported for the documented UTF-8/token framing and bounded prefix-expression contract. Public authored cases invoke Token::expressions and cover all 26 known code names, established length forms, compact and packed integers, placeholders, unary/binary operators, strings, malformed expressions, unknown tokens, and nesting limits. Raw tokens remain lossless when expressions fail. Text export is independently supported: literal tests assert exact token markers, re-encoding, UTF-8 preservation, and CSV escaping through the production sheet exporter. Structural JSON is a report, not a lossless export view. The 0xF1 token-length form still rests on one retail observation; synthetic coverage adds no retail confidence. No rendering, execution, write-back, or verified claim is established. Evidence: docs/formats/ssd-sheet.md.

formats.name: config.sys
formats.notes: The client's system settings, in the user directory rather than the install: a compiled-in stamp word, then a grid of little-endian 32-bit words holding two fixed-width UTF-16LE text spans. The one retail sample is 684 bytes, 170 words past the stamp, 50 of them written. Read to structure only: there is exactly one sample of each configuration file, so no field's meaning is claimed. A word is carried with its offset and value and a printable run is counted rather than named; the report carries the shape and never a value, because these files are the owner's own settings rather than client assets. Write is a byte-exact round trip: parsing a file and writing the model back reproduces the input byte for byte, proved by validate cases over the public fixtures and the retail files. Not claimed: what any field means, and that the client accepts a file this tool wrote after a value was changed - nothing here has been through the game. Evidence: docs/formats/configuration.md.

formats.name: config.pad
formats.notes: The client's input-device settings, the same stamped word-grid shape as config.sys, holding device identifiers and a button mapping. The one retail sample is 328 bytes, 81 words past the stamp, 14 of them written. Read to structure only: there is exactly one sample of each configuration file, so no field's meaning is claimed. A word is carried with its offset and value and a printable run is counted rather than named; the report carries the shape and never a value, because these files are the owner's own settings rather than client assets. Write is a byte-exact round trip: parsing a file and writing the model back reproduces the input byte for byte, proved by validate cases over the public fixtures and the retail files. Not claimed: what any field means, and that the client accepts a file this tool wrote after a value was changed - nothing here has been through the game. Evidence: docs/formats/configuration.md.

formats.name: config.lng
formats.notes: The client's language setting: a word grid with no stamp. The one retail sample is 8 bytes, two words. Read to structure only: there is exactly one sample of each configuration file, so no field's meaning is claimed. A word is carried with its offset and value and a printable run is counted rather than named; the report carries the shape and never a value, because these files are the owner's own settings rather than client assets. Write is a byte-exact round trip: parsing a file and writing the model back reproduces the input byte for byte, proved by validate cases over the public fixtures and the retail files. Not claimed: what any field means, and that the client accepts a file this tool wrote after a value was changed - nothing here has been through the game. Evidence: docs/formats/configuration.md.

formats.name: config.rgn
formats.notes: The client's region setting, and the thinnest row in the matrix: the one retail sample is five bytes, all zero, and is not a word grid at all. The read carries the body whole as one span with a digest and interprets nothing, which is the entire claim; there is no malformed input for it, because every byte string is a valid body. Read to structure only: there is exactly one sample of each configuration file, so no field's meaning is claimed. A printable run is counted rather than named; the report carries the shape and never a value, because these files are the owner's own settings rather than client assets. Write is a byte-exact round trip: parsing a file and writing the model back reproduces the input byte for byte, proved by validate cases over the public fixtures and the retail files. Not claimed: what any field means, and that the client accepts a file this tool wrote after a value was changed - nothing here has been through the game. Evidence: docs/formats/configuration.md.

formats.name: staticactor.san
formats.notes: Reads the retail-evidenced 13-byte header and XOR-0x73 variable-record framing, preserving the five unknown header bytes and reporting both record members without semantic names. The one retail 1.23b file has 2812 complete records and no trailing bytes. Public conformance covers the positive shape, header truncation, count bombs, missing and unterminated records, and trailing partial or complete records. Unknown header meaning, record-member meanings, string character rules, ordering and uniqueness requirements, other SAN variants, writing, and lossless export remain unresolved. Evidence: docs/formats/staticactor-san.md.

formats.name: Region definition
formats.notes: Bounded RegionResourceData 1.1.0 root/child structure, with root count at +0x24, rows at +0x40, stride 0x30, and root-only following-child count at +0x0C. Retains duplicate rows, locations, membership, token spans, and opaque field boundaries; child +0x0C is never recursive. Public cases exercise structure and concrete header/count/truncation boundaries. The pinned 52336-byte private vector accounts for 61 roots and 1089 rows ending at EOF. Unknown field meanings, token rules, native size enforcement, trailing-byte legality, and other versions remain unresolved. Writing and resource export are outside this read claim. Evidence and limits: docs/formats/region.md.

formats.name: Zone layout and collision geometry
formats.notes: Reads the documented MapLayoutResourceData table and embedded lyb graph with exact dispatched node shapes, including bounded 0x0C InstanceObject child-range descriptors and canonical five-field UnitTree groups plus the one observed exact nine-field serializer variant, bounded RES -> wrb -> MDL -> MESH -> STMS model streams for source association, structurally valid WRB resources without mesh parts, exact four-byte subtype/chunk tags, exact single-descriptor index streams, bounded four-s16 position fields, PHB.GBD hull vertices and indices with the 0x80 geometry-header and 16-byte-trailer bounds, and CollisionBox unit primitives using retail col_cube diagonal/winding. The explicit export-zones command requires a client root and output directory, emits collision-only OBJ, preserves source index order, raw PHB surfaces, and separate raw CollisionBox classification words with box raw surface 0, uses deterministic collision-safe layout-ID suffixes for duplicate normalized names, and writes version-2 compact face-range metadata sidecars plus a collection manifest with client/exporter identity, selection, classifications, source node/block IDs, resource keys, complete placement transforms, and collision bounds. Authored tests use the documented retail framing and cover decoded vertices and indices, nested placement accumulation, OBJ indexing, compact range coverage and surface splitting, duplicate naming, exact tags, and source tracing. Server-coordinate LaySettings meaning, unrecognized payload variants, render-mesh export, textures, animations, and navigation compilation remain unresolved. Evidence: docs/formats/sedb-res.md and docs/formats/zone-geometry.md.

formats.name: LPB compiled script container
formats.notes: Reads and extracts the raw and XOR-0x73 wrappers while preserving unknown header bytes. An explicit lpb-bytecode view structurally inspects an evidenced Lua 5.1 payload without changing wrapper boundaries. Unknown wrapper fields, the advisory size, unsupported wrapper variants, and LPB writing remain unresolved.

formats.name: Lua path encoding
formats.notes: Encode and decode are the same primitive pair, so write support arrives with read.

formats.name: Client Lua script payload
formats.notes: Structurally reads the evidenced official Lua 5.1 little-endian representation with 32-bit int, size_t, and instruction plus 64-bit floating number. Validates prototype-local constant, upvalue, nested-prototype, direct-register, jump, SETLIST-extra-word, and CLOSURE-binding structure under fixed resource limits. It does not build control flow, analyze reachability or liveness, simulate the stack, expose string contents, recover source, execute code, or decompile.

formats.name: GTEX texture
formats.notes: Reads the loader-backed metadata and exact offset-size surface entries. Maps observed client indices 4, 24, and 26 to D3DFMT_A8R8G8B8, D3DFMT_DXT1, and D3DFMT_DXT5 and verifies linear or block-compressed encoded size. Across 21161 retail files, all 41217 size dwords match, spans do not overlap, and final surfaces end at EOF; two adjacent pairs have explicit eight-byte gaps. Opt-in extraction materializes exact encoded surfaces or one legacy DDS containing all encoded mips for mapped table-bearing 2D textures with flags zero and depth one. DDS additionally requires nonzero dimensions and a mip count within the geometric chain. Public synthetic coverage checks standard headers, exact bytes for all three mappings, multiple mips, gaps, refusals, extraction accounting, manifest relationships, and source replay. A separate opt-in decoded top-mip PNG preview uses the same subset with a 64 MiB RGBA allocation limit. Pixel oracles cover channel order, DXT1 modes, DXT5 alpha, interpolation, and partial-block edges. PNG previews carry no lossless export status. Private DDS and PNG extract cases reproduce the three pinned standalone retail representatives. Independent checks through both extraction commands validate every raw mip, complete legacy DDS headers and payloads, and every top-mip RGBA sample under the documented conversion; inventory verification and complete source replay pass. The four supplied DXT5 mips are retained without generating the rest of the chain. Cube, volume, nonzero flags, missing tables, unmapped indices, bit-2 meaning, GTEX round-trip writing, and GPU compatibility remain unsupported. Evidence: docs/formats/gtex-pwib.md.

formats.name: PWIB tagged resource
formats.notes: Reads the exact PWIB signature and the big-endian total, first-segment, and second-segment boundaries at 0x04, 0x08, and 0x0c. It reports the SEDB-prefixed first segment and second segment independently rather than treating the first as a standalone SEDB container. All 3544 recorded retail files have ordered in-file boundaries, exact total sizes, and SEDB at the first offset. Explicit visible-entry selection handles the promoted little-endian RES/txb path with a version-one txb block, externally backed table-bearing one-mip DXT1 descriptor, 2D flags zero, and depth one. Descriptor and surface remain distinct bounded views; whole encoded ranges are checked against the second span. Raw encoded surfaces and legacy DDS reuse the GTEX byte-preserving machinery; PNG is a decoded preview without a lossless export claim. Authored coverage exercises nonzero source offsets, malformed directory and metadata extents, descriptor and surface bounds, supported-boundary refusals, both extraction commands, accounting, inventory checks and complete source replay. Other entries, variants, and remaining bytes retain spans and digests without inferred semantics. Runtime activation, appearance selection, GPU parity, and PWIB round-trip writing remain unproved. Private cases and independent artifact checks reproduce the documented m520 entry-6 vector through both extraction commands and complete source replay. Evidence: docs/formats/gtex-pwib.md.

formats.name: FDT font
formats.notes: Metadata export first; glyph rasterization is a later call.

formats.name: WRB model and mesh
formats.notes: Explicit --as wrb-model inspection and validation reuse the bounded zone model reader for RES resources with exact wrb SEDB children. Reports retain absolute chunk and stream spans, metadata, counts, digests, and opaque ranges, including valid WRB resources without MESH. Public authored cases cover accepted structure, exact tags, malformed descriptors, truncation, counts, and nesting. A pinned retail RES case authenticates the documented chunk and stream framing through independent range accounting. Generic RES inspection remains unchanged. Read is partial; structural JSON does not establish lossless export support. glTF, rendering, material and texture interpretation, skeletons, animation, and a model writer remain outside this reader. Evidence: docs/formats/wrb-model.md.

formats.name: Map layout scene graph
formats.notes: Layout reading also exists in bahamut-navmesh for its own geometry needs; the repositories do not share code or data.

formats.name: Legacy ZiPatch archive
formats.notes: FHDR, APLY, ADIR, DLED, and ETRY chunks. Modern SqPack-era chunk support is not 1.x support.
